As part of the national GIS team, you will design and maintain automation and data integration solutions for the ALTO project. You will also contribute to integrating GIS with the project's systems and data environments.

Location – Toronto, Ontario; Montréal or Québec City, Quebec.

Analyze the project's geospatial data integration, transformation, validation, and synchronization requirements.
Design, develop, test, and document reusable ETL workflows using FME Form.
Deploy, schedule, monitor, and maintain automations in FME Flow, as required.
Automate quality-control checks, anomaly detection, and validation reporting.
Integrate and synchronize data among ArcGIS Enterprise, PostgreSQL, CAD/BIM environments, and other project systems.
Develop robust logging, error-handling, alerting, and process-recovery mechanisms.
Optimize processing workflows to improve performance, scalability, and maintainability.
Troubleshoot production automation incidents and implement the necessary corrections.

Experience integrating GIS data with CAD/BIM sources, geodatabases, relational databases, files, and web services.
Proficiency in FME Form for designing, developing, testing, and optimizing complex, reusable ETL workflows.
Strong knowledge of geospatial formats, coordinate systems, data schemas, validation rules, and data-quality principles.
Strong command of SQL in PostgreSQL; knowledge of Python, REST APIs, web services, and version-control practices is considered an asset.
Ability to document requirements, architecture, processing logic, tests, dependencies, and support procedures.
Proficiency in French or English; French–English bilingualism is a significant asset because of collaboration with teams in Quebec and elsewhere in Canada.*
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills for designing reliable and efficient automations.
Rigour in development, testing, documentation, and change management.
Independence and accountability when supporting automated production processes.

jobs.description:
About The Role

Balfour Beatty are looking for a Senior Geo-Environmental Engineer to join thier Power T&D Division in Derby.

Role Purpose

Providing technical support, advice, strategy and direction to the geotechnical and geo-environmental team leader and wider team.

You will deliver integrated site assessments that inform planning, design and remediation strategies.

You will work with the project team, designers and subcontractors through the design phase to deliver safe and suitable scope of works in line with the project objectives and then deliver these to a high standard.

The role includes leading Phase 1 and 2 site and ground investigations and ensuring the production of high-quality technical reporting deliverables, and the development of practical, cost-effective remediation approaches to all projects secured by Balfour Beatty Power Transmission and Distribution (BB PT&D).

Balfour Beatty welcomes applications from both full-time and part-time candidates, including those interested in job-sharing arrangements. Additionally, the company offers a flexible working policy to support a healthy work-life balance.

What you'll be doing

Key Accountabilities

To undertake Phase 1 and Phase 2 geotechnical and geo-environmental assessment as required for OHL, Cabling and Substation projects, from the initial feasibility assessment, through desk study phase and design development to detailed design & delivery / construction phase and scheme closure ensuring completion in accordance with programme, cost and quality requirements.
Ensure the timely and quality delivery of designs to meet budget, programme and pre-determined objectives. Preparation of reports, calculations and drawings to a high technical level which are compliant with the required Client and national technical standards (BS/Eurocodes/ENA).
Checking of other work packages

Key Responsibilities

Design appropriate investigation works to allow for a detailed land contamination assessment and plan for remedial works to suitably remediate contaminated land where proven to exist. Including:

Lead start-to-end delivery of Phase 1 Feasibility and Desktop Studies, Phase 2 Ground Investigations, and follow on remediation strategy and verification works.
Manage multi-disciplinary ground investigations, integrating geotechnical and geo-environmental in-situ and laboratory based test results and other data provision, management and assessments.
Produce GI specifications and schedules and where required contract documents, manage GI contractors and support with exploratory hole termination advice and decisions, installation design and details, sampling, backfill and scheduling of geotechnical and chemical laboratory testing schedules.
Produce high quality and comprehensive geotechnical and geo-environmental factual and interpretative reports, undertake contamination risk assessments with evaluation of ground conditions and design parameters where necessary.
Provide technical input into foundation and infrastructure assessment and design, ground improvement strategies, and remediation schemes
Build and maintain close and strong working relationships with clients, consultants and regulatory bodies.
Schedule chemical testing , analyse and present findings of contamination assessments clearly and support clients to satisfying planning and other regulatory conditions and achieve environmental compliance
Provide on site assessment of geological conditions resulting in design decisions for applicable engineering solutions.
Undertake assessment on the condition and nature of materials and advise on their acceptability for re-use.
Prepare accurate costings, monitor budgets, and drive efficient and timely project delivery in the team.
Appoint, liaise with and manage subcontractors to support delivery of their reports and deliverables.
Devise training plans to upskill and support junior engineers in the team and staff across to be competent in areas of environmental and land contamination assessment including line management responsibilities?
Working closely with Project Teams to determine and maintain common objectives and to ensure work undertaken is appropriate and in accordance with project priorities.
Embed “Safety by Design” principles in all activities, including managing safety through appropriate life cycle designs that minimise risks to personnel and property, by ensuring that Health & Safety Regulations and Balfour Beatty procedures and requirements are followed in the design substation, cabling and OHL projects.

Who we're looking for

Skills Required

Degree level education or equivalent with formal training in geology, civil engineering and/or geotechnical engineering.
Professional membership of either the ICE or Geol Soc & working towards Chartered Engineer status with the aim of achieving this within the next year to two years maximum period of time.
Experience of coordinating with government agencies and local authorities such as SEPA, EA etc
Strong, proven post-graduate track record and level of experience in the civil engineering industry
Proven experience in both geotechnical and geo-environmental project delivery.
Strong technical report writing skills, including Phase 1 & 2 desk study and GIR assessments
Working knowledge of remediation processes and environmental modelling
Practical understanding of ground conditions and foundation types and behaviour
Experience of the supervision and/or monitoring of sub-contractors
Proven experience of the design of large scale civil engineering works
Strong, proven experience of the management of design of civil or geotechnical engineering works
IT Literate (Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel)
Extensive experience of geotechnical design software including slope and retention design packages

Why work for us

Day in, day out, our teams deliver some of the UK’s most ambitious, exciting and meaningful projects; developing, building and maintaining the vital infrastructure that supports national economies and strengthens communities.

Benefits

As if contributing to and supporting work that makes life better for millions wasn’t rewarding enough, we offer a full range of benefits too. You’ll have the freedom to shape the package that’s right for you and your life. Here are some of our key benefits:

Smart working, giving you more flexibility such as staggered start and finish times, with up to 40% remote working, where roles allow.
25 days paid annual leave (pro rata)
Family friendly policies which include 28 weeks full pay for maternity/adoption leave and four weeks full pay for paternity/partners leave
Pension, share incentive plan, volunteering leave, recognition schemes and much more…

About Us

Balfour Beatty’s Power Transmission & Distribution teams work with regional, national and international electricity network owners and operators to provide technical engineering solutions across the full spectrum of the electricity grid, including overhead lines, cabling, substations and distribution networks.

From scoping and feasibility, to design, construction and on-going maintenance, our in-house experts, flexible resources and industry-leading innovations support customers in the development of some of the UK’s most ambitious power transmission and distribution projects.

Diversity and inclusion

At Balfour Beatty we believe that diversity and inclusion are essential components of any successful, happy workplace. Through our Value Everyone Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, we are growing our diverse workforce and developing our inclusive culture where everyone is able to thrive and reach their full potential, regardless of their identity or background. To find out how we are making this a reality, visit www.balfourbeatty.com/diversityandinclusion

The Vacancy

We have an exciting opportunity for a Principal Geo-Environmental Consultant
to join RSK Geosciences
in Bristol
. Working alongside an experienced and growing team based UK-wide, you will get involved with a wide variety of geo-environmental projects covering sectors including energy infrastructure, renewables (solar/ wind) and development/ regeneration projects. .

What you can expect in this position:

As a senior member of the team you will be expected to lead or assist in the delivery of geo-environmental projects. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong technical capabilities and will be expected to assist with technical review of geo-environmental reports from the outset. It is expected that employees working at this grade will have a keen project finance awareness, be client facing, self-motivated, exhibit a proactive approach.

The successful candidate may base themselves out of RSK Geosciences offices in Bristol, and there may be opportunities to work occasionally out of other RSK offices or from home in hybrid form. This role is available as a full-time position however a part time position will be considered.

Designing geo-environmental investigation projects and project director/lead for larger complex sites including the technical review of tenders and project reports.
Peer review of third party reports against regulatory standards and good practice.
Working with technical and projects leads to deliver appropriate solutions on geo-environmental matters in development, Part IIA, permitting (EPR/ PPC/ WML) and other relevant sectors.
Supporting the wider RSK Geosciences team and technical leads by preparing and technically reviewing technical notes, drawings and reports and sharing knowledge through preparing and delivering seminars and training.
Communicating with colleagues, clients (both external and within the wider RSK Group) and stakeholders to build strong working relationships with the aim of meeting and exceeding client expectations, encouraging repeat business and contributing to a strong team ethic.
Supporting business development by promoting RSK Geosciences to the wider industry and attending and presenting at relevant events.

Stewardship of health, safety and environment in accordance with company standards and contribute to sustainability goals.
Coaching and mentoring others within the geosciences team.

Strong technical, commercial and project management capabilities.
Practical experience in design, management and interpretation of geo-environmental site investigations.

Proactive and a self-starter, able to work independently and within teams face to face and remotely.
Client driven with the ability to motivate and engage with immediate colleagues, those across the wider RSK business and externally in conferences, events etc.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including report writing.
Strong analytical skills and close attention to detail.
Ability to multi-task, plan and prioritise workload.
Computer literate and skilled with Microsoft Office applications, in particular Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Experience of using Microsoft Project also valuable.
Full UK driving licence.

BSc degree level qualified in Geology, Chemistry, Environmental Science or similar.

The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies is responsible for the overall direction, planning, coordination, and implementation of a scientific research program that supports and is aligned with the conservation objectives and strategy of the SDZWA. Scientific disciplines practiced within the Biotechnologies department include cryogenic biobanking of living cells and gametes (which comprise the SDZWA Frozen Zoo®), advanced population genomics, advanced reproductive technologies, cell biology, endocrinology, stem cell biology, bioinformatics and more. We are seeking a visionary conservation science leader who brings deep scientific expertise, a track record of innovation, and the ability to translate integrative science into transformative conservation outcomes. The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies is responsible for the overall direction, planning, coordination, and implementation of a scientific research program that supports and is aligned with the conservation objectives and strategy of the SDZWA. The Conservation Biotechnologies department takes an integrative and innovative approach; applying an array of scientific disciplines to support strategies (e.g., genetic rescue, population assessment and management, assisted reproduction) designed to safeguard and restore biodiversity and to manage wildlife populations in situ and ex situ. Scientific disciplines practiced within the Biotechnologies department include cryogenic biobanking of living cells and gametes (which comprise the SDZWA Frozen Zoo®), advanced population genomics, advanced reproductive technologies, cell biology, endocrinology, stem cell biology, bioinformatics and more. The Director of Conservation Biotechnologies is a subject-matter expert in either conservation genetics/genomics, reproductive sciences, cellular biology, or biodiversity banking, with a high level of fluency in the other disciplines. This position requires a proven track record of innovating, applying, and critically evaluating scientific approaches for biodiversity conservation, as well as a strong record of collaboration across sectors.
As a leadership position in the Conservation Science Wildlife Health (CSWH) department, the Director of Conservation Biotechnologies communicates the SDZWA conservation vision and strategy to their team, identifies and prioritizes projects that strengthen connections with other teams in CSWH, departments within SDZWA, external partners, and has a working knowledge of approaches/tools used by the SDZWA to ensure activities support conservation outcomes (e.g., The Conservation Standards). The Director is a member of the Conservation Science leadership team, and is responsible for monitoring, reporting, and communicating the Conservation Biotechnology team's conservation and science outcomes. The Director will contribute to organizational conservation strategic planning and fundraising, including securing grant funding through various sources.
Additional responsibilities of the Director of Conservation Biotechnologies include budget development and oversight, internal and external communications, ensuring that the team complies with ethical, safety and other guidelines as defined by SDZWA policies and procedures. Job Description

Kuna is looking for an Environmental Monitoring and Regulatory Compliance Professional to embed at the Red Dog Mine for 2 week on and 2 week off shifts. This position is scheduled to last into April 2027. The work may be extended as required by the client.

Responsibilities

Provide environmental support to on-going civil construction projects.
Monitor construction and ensure compliance with permits and regulations.
Permits include Construction Rock Handling, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plans, Multi-Sector General Permits, Cultural Resources Protection and Monitoring Plans, and Nesting Bird Standard Operating Procedures.

Document compliance with plans, policies, procedures, and permit requirements.
Complete inspections, monitor data sheets, and reporting forms.
Coordinate between the construction manager and the construction teams to facilitate communication and quickly resolve conflicts, issues, and challenges related to environmental concerns that may arise in the field.
This position has no supervisory responsibilities.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in encironmental sciences, engineering, chemistry, natural resource management, or related field.
Minimum three (3) years’ experience in construction environmental monitoring and management, preferably in mining or road construction.
Practical experience in erosion prevention and sediment control for construction projects, and turbidity monitoring and sampling; AK-CESCL certification/credentials desired.
Knowledge of applicable regulatory, legal, and other requirements.
Working knowledge of arctic wildlife and vegetation management.
Experience working under US and State of Alaska environmental statutes/regulations/permits.
Strong technical skills and the practical ability to solve problems.
Ability to work in a team environment and work effectively across all levels of the business.
Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record for the past three (3) years to be eligible under company vehicle insurance policy.

Competencies

Professional, highly self-motivated, passionate, energetic, creative and strategic thinker.
Dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of internal and external customers.
Always acts with customers in mind, knows how to establish and maintain effective relationships with customers/prospects and gains their trust and respect.
Desire to improve personally, increasing ability and skillset.

Weather: Indoors/Outdoors – Frequent exposure to moderate to harsh weather conditions. Requires work to be done both inside and outside.

Noise level: The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Description of environment: Frequently required to be outside at construction/project sites. Also occasionally inside in standard office setting.

Physical requirements: Employee is required to occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 lbs. Frequently required to sit, stand, walk, use hands/fingers to handle or feel, climb, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, talk/hear, see, taste/smell, and carry weight/lift.

Travel: May travel 100 percent of the time during field season and be away on field trips for multiple days. Employee may travel to remote areas and may be required to use alternative modes of transportation, including but not limited to snow machines, boats, small airplanes, helicopters and ATVs.

Travel may require an employee or contractor to pass a TSA security checkpoint. If the employee or contractor does not have valid identification, they will not be able to travel until valid identification is obtained and verified. For this reason all employees and contractors must have valid identification when traveling to and from the work site destination, for a list of TSA approved valid identification visit https://www.tsa.gov/travel/security-screening/identification .
